title: Cross-module reads in visits.js, appointments.js and prescriptions.js — port requirements for the .NET modular monolith

findings.name: PhysicianProfile lookup by userId (the single most repeated cross-module read)
findings.signature: prisma.physicianProfile.findUnique({ where: { userId } })  — no select, full row
findings.behaviour: Appears ~35 times. visits.js: GET /specialty-template (reads .specialty), GET / (.id), POST / (.id), GET /:id (.id, wrapped in .catch(()=>null)), PUT /:id, PUT /:id/complete, POST /:id/generate-soap (.id + .specialty), POST /:id/transcribe, POST /:id/suggest-codes, POST|PUT|DELETE /:id/investigations, GET /follow-ups-due, DELETE /:id. appointments.js: GET /slots, POST /slots, DELETE /slots/:id, POST /slots/bulk, POST /slots/sync-from-hours, GET / , GET /today, POST /walk-in, PUT /:id/confirm|cancel|complete|no-show, DELETE /:id, PUT /:id/check-in, POST /:id/intake-note, GET /ai-optimize. prescriptions.js: GET /, GET /summary, GET /interaction-history, GET /:id, PUT /:id, PUT /:id/sign, PUT /:id/send, PUT /:id/dispense, PUT /:id/refill-respond, POST /check-interactions, GET /:id/pdf, POST /transcribe-rx, POST /extract-from-plan. Only .id and .specialty are ever read; the row is NEVER put in a response body. Missing-profile behaviour differs per endpoint and must be preserved exactly: GET /visits returns {data:[],pagination:{total:0,page,limit,pages:0}}; GET /appointments, GET /appointments/slots, GET /appointments/today, GET /prescriptions, GET /prescriptions/interaction-history return []; GET /visits/follow-ups-due returns []; GET /visits/specialty-template returns {template:null, allTemplates:[]} (note: NO `specialty` key on this branch); GET /prescriptions/summary returns {signed:0,sent:0,total:0}; POST /visits and POST /appointments/slots* return 400 {error:'Physician profile required'}; GET /appointments/ai-optimize returns 403; POST /prescriptions/transcribe-rx returns 403 {error:'Only physicians can dictate prescriptions'}; POST /prescriptions/extract-from-plan returns 403 {error:'Only physicians can extract prescriptions'}.
findings.portRecommendation: COVERED by the existing IIdentityDirectory.GetPhysicianByUserIdAsync — PhysicianSummary carries Id and Specialty. No new port. Every Visits/Appointments/Prescriptions handler resolves the caller's physician through this and must never touch PhysicianProfile via a DbContext.

findings.name: PhysicianProfile lookup BY PROFILE ID to resolve the owning userId (for notifications)
findings.signature: prisma.physicianProfile.findUnique({ where: { id: <physicianProfileId> }, select: { userId: true } })
findings.behaviour: Used to convert a physicianId (profile id, stored on Visit/Appointment/Prescription) into the User id that a notification is addressed to. visits.js PUT /:id/patient-feedback (notifies physician of patient feedback; skips notification entirely if the profile is missing). appointments.js POST /walk-in — called TWICE in the same request (once for the PATIENT_ARRIVED notification, once again for WaitingQueue.physicianUserId), and the notification is suppressed when physicianProfile.userId === the caller's userId. appointments.js PUT /:id/cancel (patient cancelled → notify physician). prescriptions.js POST /:id/refill-request. All are inside try/catch — a failure never fails the request.
findings.portRecommendation: COVERED, awkwardly, by IIdentityDirectory.GetPhysiciansAsync(new[]{id}) which is keyed by profile id. RECOMMEND adding a singular convenience to the existing port rather than a new one: Task<PhysicianSummary?> GetPhysicianAsync(string physicianProfileId, CancellationToken ct = default); on IIdentityDirectory (Identity module owns the implementation). Do NOT add a Visits/Appointments-local shortcut.

findings.name: PhysicianProfile FULL ROW + nested user.displayName serialized into the queue response
findings.signature: include: { physician: { include: { user: { select: { displayName: true } } } } }
findings.behaviour: This is an `include`, not a `select`, so EVERY PhysicianProfile scalar column is spread into the JSON that goes out on GET /api/appointments/queue: physician: { id, userId, licenseNumber, specialty, qualifications, bio, scratchpadNotes, yearsOfExperience, verified, verifiedAt (ISO string|null), createdAt (ISO string), updatedAt (ISO string), user: { displayName } }. Two consequences for the port: (a) PhysicianSummary is INSUFFICIENT — it lacks Qualifications, Bio, ScratchpadNotes, YearsOfExperience, VerifiedAt, CreatedAt, UpdatedAt; (b) the physician's private scratchpadNotes and bio are exposed to any active clinic staff member (receptionist) who calls this endpoint. Byte-identical JSON requires reproducing this leak. Contrast with PUT /:id/check-in and POST /:id/intake-note, which also `include` the physician but respond with the freshly-updated row instead, so the physician object does NOT reach the client there.
findings.portRecommendation: NEW result record on the EXISTING port, owned by Identity: add `Task<IReadOnlyDictionary<string, PhysicianDetail>> GetPhysicianDetailsAsync(IReadOnlyCollection<string> physicianProfileIds, CancellationToken ct = default)` to IIdentityDirectory, returning `sealed record PhysicianDetail(string Id, string UserId, string LicenseNumber, string Specialty, string? Qualifications, string? Bio, string? ScratchpadNotes, int? YearsOfExperience, bool Verified, DateTime? VerifiedAt, DateTime CreatedAt, DateTime UpdatedAt, string DisplayName)`. The Appointments queue response DTO then serializes it with the exact Prisma key order and a nested `user: { displayName }` object.

findings.name: PhysicianProfile → Clinic ownership join (physician owns THIS clinic)
findings.signature: prisma.physicianProfile.findUnique({ where: { userId }, include: { clinics: { where: { id: clinicId }, take: 1 } } });  isPhysician = physician && physician.clinics.length > 0
findings.behaviour: Grants queue access only when the caller's physician profile OWNS the requested clinic. If not, falls back to an active ClinicStaff row; otherwise 403 {error:'Not staff at this clinic'}. Requires ?clinicId, else 400 {error:'clinicId required'}.
findings.portRecommendation: NEW port method — and do NOT reuse IClinicAccessEvaluator here. IClinicAccessEvaluator mirrors server/src/middleware/clinicPermission.js, whose precedence is 'owning physician → ANY physician profile → staff row'. These three route files never use that middleware; they use the strictly narrower 'owns this clinic' / 'physicianId matches this record' test. Substituting the evaluator would let any physician with a profile read any clinic's queue. Add to a new IClinicDirectory (Clinics module): Task<bool> IsOwningPhysicianAsync(string clinicId, string physicianProfileId, CancellationToken ct = default).

findings.name: Clinic ownership guard before slot mutation
findings.signature: prisma.clinic.findFirst({ where: { id: clinicId, physicianId: physician.id } })
findings.behaviour: Full row fetched, used as a truthiness guard in the appointments cases — 403 {error:'Not your clinic'} when null. Note it does NOT filter isActive, so an inactive clinic still passes. In visits.js POST / the row is also used for its data: `clinic.organizationId` is copied onto the new Visit's organizationId, so Visits genuinely needs a clinic field, not just a boolean.
findings.portRecommendation: NEW port IClinicDirectory (Clinics module owns it, published in SharedKernel/Abstractions/Directory alongside IIdentityDirectory): Task<ClinicSummary?> GetClinicAsync(string clinicId, CancellationToken ct = default) and Task<bool> IsOwningPhysicianAsync(string clinicId, string physicianProfileId, CancellationToken ct = default). ClinicSummary must carry OrganizationId and PhysicianId for the visit-creation path.

findings.name: Clinic scalar projections embedded in Visit / Appointment / Prescription response payloads
findings.signature: include: { clinic: { select: { ... } } } — six DIFFERENT projections
findings.behaviour: Each endpoint ships a different subset, and the key set is part of the contract: GET /visits → clinic:{id,name,specialty}; GET /visits/:id → clinic:{id,name,specialty,phone}; POST /visits → clinic:{name} (NO id); GET /appointments/slots and GET /appointments/available → clinic:{name}; GET /appointments → clinic:{id,name,address,phone}; GET /appointments/today, POST /appointments, POST /appointments/walk-in → clinic:{name}; PUT /appointments/:id/check-in → clinic:{id,name} but internal only (the response is the re-fetched updated row, so no clinic key goes out); GET /prescriptions → visit.clinic:{name}; GET /prescriptions/:id → visit.clinic:{name,phone,address}; GET /prescriptions/:id/pdf → visit.clinic:{name,address,city,phone,logo} (HTML response, not JSON). Every one of these is non-null in practice (clinicId is a required FK) but must serialize as a nested object, never flattened.
findings.portRecommendation: NEW port IClinicDirectory (Clinics module). Batch-first to avoid N+1: Task<IReadOnlyDictionary<string, ClinicSummary>> GetClinicsAsync(IReadOnlyCollection<string> clinicIds, CancellationToken ct = default), with `sealed record ClinicSummary(string Id, string OrganizationId, string PhysicianId, string Name, string? Address, string? City, string? Country, string? Phone, string? Email, string? Specialty, string? Logo, bool IsActive, bool AllowPatientBooking, double? ConsultationFee, double? FollowUpFee, string? WorkingHours)`. One superset record; each endpoint's response DTO projects the exact subset above.

findings.name: Clinic.allowPatientBooking gate on the availability endpoint
findings.signature: prisma.clinic.findUnique({ where: { id: clinicId }, select: { allowPatientBooking: true, physicianId: true } })
findings.behaviour: Only runs when ?clinicId is supplied. When the clinic exists and allowPatientBooking is false, the caller must be the physician themselves (req.user.id === physicianUserId query param) or hold an active ClinicStaff row at that clinic; otherwise the endpoint returns an EMPTY ARRAY [] with HTTP 200 — never a 403. A missing clinic row silently skips the whole gate. `physicianId` is selected but never used.
findings.portRecommendation: COVERED by the proposed IClinicDirectory.GetClinicAsync (AllowPatientBooking is on ClinicSummary). The staff half needs the ClinicStaff membership port below.

findings.name: Clinic consultation/follow-up fees for auto-created check-in payment
findings.signature: prisma.clinic.findUnique({ where: { id: appt.clinicId }, select: { id: true, consultationFee: true, followUpFee: true } })
findings.behaviour: Inside a swallowing try/catch. If the clinic row is missing the whole payment block is skipped and the response's `payment` key is null. Fee selection: isFollowUp = (count of COMPLETED visits for this clinicId+patientUserId > 0); fee = isFollowUp ? (clinic.followUpFee || 200) : (clinic.consultationFee || 300). The `|| 200 / || 300` fallbacks fire on null AND on a stored 0. A payment is created only when no Payment row already exists for this appointmentId AND fee > 0.
findings.portRecommendation: COVERED by IClinicDirectory.GetClinicAsync (ConsultationFee, FollowUpFee on ClinicSummary). Reproduce the `||` fallback as `(fee is null or 0) ? 200/300 : fee` — a C# `??` would NOT match, because 0 falls through in JS.

findings.name: Clinic.workingHours WRITE — the working-hours source for POST /slots/sync-from-hours
findings.signature: prisma.clinic.update({ where: { id: clinicId }, data: { workingHours: JSON.stringify(schedule) } })
findings.behaviour: CRITICAL: this endpoint does NOT read working hours from anywhere. The schedule is supplied in the REQUEST BODY (`{ clinicId, schedule: [{dayOfWeek,startTime,endTime,slotDuration}] }`); the only clinic read is the ownership guard. The clinic is the WRITE target, and it is a cross-module write from Appointments into Clinics. The stored value is `JSON.stringify(schedule)` — a JSON *string* written into a Prisma `Json?` column, i.e. double-encoded. This is load-bearing: client/src/pages/ClinicDetailPage.jsx:82 does `JSON.parse(response.data.workingHours)` when re-reading GET /clinics/:id, while clinics.js:1091 writes the raw object for the same column. The .NET port MUST store the serialized string, not the array, or the clinic schedule editor breaks. Full flow: 400 if !clinicId || !Array.isArray(schedule); 400 'Physician profile required'; 403 'Not your clinic'; then timeSlot.deleteMany({physicianId, clinicId}) — ALL days wiped, unlike /slots/bulk which wipes one day; then expands each entry into slots of `slotDuration || 15` minutes (note: default 15 here, 30 in /slots/bulk) with `while (currentMinutes + duration <= endMinutes)`; entries missing dayOfWeek/startTime/endTime are silently skipped (`continue`); the clinic.update runs even when zero slots were produced. Response: HTTP 200 (not 201, unlike /slots and /slots/bulk) { count, message: `${count} slots created` }.
findings.portRecommendation: NEW write port, and it is the only write-side clinic port needed here. Owned by the Clinics module, published as IClinicWorkingHoursWriter in SharedKernel/Abstractions/Directory: Task<bool> SetWorkingHoursAsync(string clinicId, string? workingHoursJson, CancellationToken ct = default). Pass the already-serialized JSON string so the double-encoding stays explicit and reviewable at the call site.

findings.name: ClinicStaff membership check — 'is this user active staff at this clinic'
findings.signature: prisma.clinicStaff.findFirst({ where: { userId, clinicId, isActive: true } })
findings.behaviour: Eleven call sites in appointments.js, all pure truthiness guards (the row's role/permissions Json is fetched but never inspected). Used at: GET /available (bypass allowPatientBooking), GET / (clinic-scoped staff listing — from `req.headers['x-clinic-id'] || req.query.clinicId`; when the staff row exists `where.clinicId = staffClinicId`, otherwise it silently falls back to `where.patientUserId = userId`), POST /walk-in (resolve physician via the clinic when the caller has no physician profile; 403 'Not authorized' when absent), PUT /:id/confirm, PUT /:id/cancel, PUT /:id/complete, PUT /:id/no-show, DELETE /:id, PUT /:id/check-in, POST /:id/intake-note, GET /queue. Each is short-circuited by `!isPhysician` (or `!isPhysician && !isPatient`), so the query does not run when the caller already qualifies. QUIRK: the JSDoc on PUT /:id/check-in and POST /:id/intake-note claims 'clinic staff with canDraftNotes', but NO permission key is ever evaluated — any active staff row of any role passes.
findings.portRecommendation: NEW port method, NOT IClinicAccessEvaluator (see the GET /queue finding — the evaluator grants to any physician profile and would widen access). Add to IClinicDirectory (Clinics module): Task<bool> IsActiveStaffAsync(string userId, string clinicId, CancellationToken ct = default).

findings.name: ClinicStaff roster — every active staff userId at a clinic, for the visit-completed fan-out
findings.signature: prisma.clinicStaff.findMany({ where: { clinicId: visit.clinicId, isActive: true }, select: { userId: true } })
findings.behaviour: The ONLY ClinicStaff read in visits.js. Sends one VISIT_COMPLETED_STAFF notification per staff member, sequentially (await inside a for-loop), with message `${patientUser?.displayName || 'Patient'}'s visit is done${followUpText}` where followUpText is ` — Follow-up: ${new Date(updated.followUpDate).toLocaleDateString()}` or ''. Note the message embeds a LOCALE-FORMATTED date from the server's default locale (no explicit locale argument) — the .NET port must match the Node runtime's formatting or the notification text drifts. data payload: { visitId, patientUserId, followUpDate (Date, serialized to ISO in the Json column), clinicId }. sendEmail is not set (defaults false). Whole block is wrapped in a swallowing try/catch and never fails the request.
findings.portRecommendation: NEW port method on IClinicDirectory (Clinics module): Task<IReadOnlyList<string>> ListActiveStaffUserIdsAsync(string clinicId, CancellationToken ct = default). Returns an empty list, never null, when there is no staff.

findings.name: ClinicPatient — display projections embedded in Visit responses
findings.signature: include: { clinicPatient: { select: { id, name, phone } } } | { select: { name } }; prisma.clinicPatient.findUnique({ where: { id }, select: { name, phone, email } })
findings.behaviour: ClinicPatient is the physician-owned local chart used when the patient has no Tebrazi account. GET /visits: the raw `clinicPatient:{id,name,phone}` object stays in the payload AND drives a reshape — for rows with a clinicPatient the handler emits `patientUser: { displayName: cp.name, phone: cp.phone }` (only 2 keys, NO id, NO email), whereas User-backed rows emit `patientUser: { id, displayName, email }` (3 keys, NO phone). The client therefore receives two structurally different patientUser shapes from the same array — this asymmetry must be reproduced exactly. GET /visits/:id normalizes both to `{ displayName, email, phone }` (from ClinicPatient: displayName←name, email←email, phone←phone; null when the clinicPatient row is missing). POST /visits returns `clinicPatient:{id,name,phone}` or null. GET /follow-ups-due uses `clinicPatient:{name}` only to pick patientName, preferring it over the User lookup. GET /prescriptions/:id/pdf uses `visit.clinicPatient.name` as the second choice for the printed patient name (subprofile first, clinicPatient second, User third, literal 'Patient' last).
findings.portRecommendation: NEW module + NEW port. ClinicPatient has no .NET home yet; recommend the CLINICS module own it (it is keyed by physicianUserId + clinicId and lives alongside PatientTag/PatientNote as the clinic's own roster — it is not a PatientProfile). Publish IClinicPatientDirectory in SharedKernel/Abstractions/Directory: Task<ClinicPatientSummary?> GetAsync(string id, CancellationToken ct); Task<IReadOnlyDictionary<string, ClinicPatientSummary>> GetManyAsync(IReadOnlyCollection<string> ids, CancellationToken ct); with `sealed record ClinicPatientSummary(string Id, string PhysicianUserId, string? ClinicId, string Name, string? Phone, string? Email, DateTime? DateOfBirth, string? Gender, string? LinkedUserId, bool IsActive, DateTime? LastVisitDate)`.

findings.name: ClinicPatient.linkedUserId resolution when creating a visit for a local chart
findings.signature: prisma.clinicPatient.findUnique({ where: { id: clinicPatientId } });  resolvedPatientUserId = cp?.linkedUserId || userId
findings.behaviour: Only runs when clinicPatientId is supplied AND patientUserId is not. QUIRK WITH REAL DATA CONSEQUENCES: when the chart has no linked account (or the id does not resolve), patientUserId falls back to `userId` — the PHYSICIAN'S OWN user id — as a placeholder. Every downstream consumer inherits this: the visit appears in the physician's own patient-side visit list, PUT /:id/complete sends the VISIT_COMPLETED notification to the physician, and PUT /:id/patient-feedback treats the physician as the patient. The .NET port must reproduce it, not 'fix' it. Note the lookup does not filter isActive.
findings.portRecommendation: COVERED by the proposed IClinicPatientDirectory.GetAsync (LinkedUserId on ClinicPatientSummary).

findings.name: ClinicPatient.lastVisitDate WRITE from the Visits module
findings.signature: prisma.clinicPatient.update({ where: { id: clinicPatientId }, data: { lastVisitDate: new Date() } }).catch(() => {})
findings.behaviour: Fire-and-forget cross-module write: stamps the chart's lastVisitDate at visit creation (not at completion). Errors are swallowed by a bare .catch — a missing chart id never fails the 201. Runs whenever clinicPatientId was supplied, including the case where the linkedUserId fallback above kicked in.
findings.portRecommendation: NEW write method on the same port, kept explicitly narrow so Visits cannot mutate anything else: on IClinicPatientDirectory add Task TouchLastVisitAsync(string clinicPatientId, DateTime visitedAtUtc, CancellationToken ct = default). Owned by Clinics. Must not throw on a missing row.

findings.name: FamilySubprofile — display projections embedded in Visit / Appointment / Prescription responses
findings.signature: include: { subprofile: { select: { id, name, relation } } } | { name, relation } | { name } | { name, relation, dateOfBirth }
findings.behaviour: Four distinct projections, all nullable (subprofileId is optional), all serialized as a nested object or JSON null: GET /visits → subprofile:{id,name,relation}; POST /visits → {name,relation}; GET /visits/:id → {id,name,relation} — and in the fallback path (when the full include throws) the handler FORCES `visit.subprofile = null` and `visit.investigations = []`, so a degraded response silently drops the subprofile; GET /visits/follow-ups-due → {name} used to emit `subprofileName: v.subprofile?.name` (UNDEFINED, therefore the key is OMITTED from the JSON entirely when there is no subprofile — not null); GET /appointments, POST /appointments, GET /appointments/today, GET /appointments/queue → {name,relation}; GET /prescriptions, GET /prescriptions/:id/pdf → {name,relation}; GET /prescriptions/:id → {name,relation,dateOfBirth} where dateOfBirth is a Date serialized as a full ISO-8601 string (or null). POST /appointments additionally reads `appointment.subprofile.name` to build the notification text ` (for ${name})`. `relation` is the SubprofileRelation enum, emitted as its bare string name (SELF/SPOUSE/CHILD/...).
findings.portRecommendation: NEW port IPatientDirectory (Patients module owns it, published in SharedKernel/Abstractions/Directory). Batch-first: Task<IReadOnlyDictionary<string, SubprofileSummary>> GetSubprofilesAsync(IReadOnlyCollection<string> subprofileIds, CancellationToken ct = default) plus a singular Task<SubprofileSummary?> GetSubprofileAsync(string id, CancellationToken ct = default); `sealed record SubprofileSummary(string Id, string PatientProfileId, string Name, string Relation, DateTime? DateOfBirth, string? Gender, string? BloodType, bool IsActive)`. One superset record; each response DTO projects its exact subset, and the follow-ups-due DTO must OMIT subprofileName rather than emit null.

findings.name: FamilySubprofile clinical bundle (allergies + active conditions + active medications) for SOAP context
findings.signature: prisma.familySubprofile.findUnique({ where: { id: visit.subprofileId }, include: { allergies: true, conditions: { where: { isActive: true } }, medications: { where: { isActive: true } } } })
findings.behaviour: Builds the AI prompt's patient-context block (never returned to the client). Reads sub.name, sub.relation, allergies[].allergen, allergies[].severity, conditions[].condition (the correct field name), medications[].drugName, medications[].dosage. Formatting is exact and must be reproduced because it changes AI output: 'Patient: {name} ({relation})' / 'Allergies: {allergen} ({severity||'unknown'}), ...' or 'None documented' / 'Chronic Conditions: {condition}, ...' or 'None documented' / 'Current Medications: {drugName} {dosage||''}, ...' or 'None documented', joined by newlines. QUIRK: `allergies: true` applies NO filter at all — Allergy has no isActive column, and deletedAt is NOT excluded either, so soft-deleted allergies leak into the prompt. Conditions and medications filter isActive but likewise ignore deletedAt. Skipped entirely when visit.subprofileId is null; the whole block is in a bare try/catch that continues without context.
findings.portRecommendation: NEW method on IPatientDirectory (Patients module): Task<SubprofileClinicalContext?> GetSubprofileClinicalContextAsync(string subprofileId, CancellationToken ct = default) returning `sealed record SubprofileClinicalContext(string Name, string Relation, IReadOnlyList<AllergyItem> Allergies, IReadOnlyList<string> Conditions, IReadOnlyList<MedicationItem> Medications)` with `record AllergyItem(string Allergen, string? Severity)` and `record MedicationItem(string DrugName, string? Dosage)`. The implementation must deliberately NOT filter deletedAt on allergies, and must filter only IsActive on conditions/medications, to keep the prompt byte-identical.

findings.name: FamilySubprofile ids for a patient user, resolved through PatientProfile
findings.signature: prisma.familySubprofile.findMany({ where: { patientProfile: { userId: patientUserId } }, select: { id: true } });  prisma.familySubprofile.findFirst({ where: { patientProfile: { userId: patientUserId } }, select: { id: true } })
findings.behaviour: A relation filter that traverses FamilySubprofile → PatientProfile → userId, i.e. a two-table join entirely inside the Patients module. findMany (only when no subprofileId was supplied) drives a per-subprofile CurrentMedication loop; findFirst picks ONE subprofile for the allergy/condition context. QUIRKS: findFirst has NO orderBy, so the 'representative' subprofile is whatever the database returns first — non-deterministic across engines; and neither query filters isActive, so inactive subprofiles are included.
findings.portRecommendation: NEW method on IPatientDirectory (Patients module): Task<IReadOnlyList<string>> ListSubprofileIdsByUserAsync(string patientUserId, CancellationToken ct = default). Take the first element for the findFirst case rather than adding a second method; to stay deterministic in SQL Server, order by Id and accept that it may differ from Postgres — flag this as a documented divergence, since the affected code path is already dead (see the Allergy/ChronicCondition finding).

findings.name: CurrentMedication — active drug names by subprofile
findings.signature: prisma.currentMedication.findMany({ where: { subprofileId, isActive: true }, select: { drugName: true } })
findings.behaviour: Two call sites. (1) When the caller supplies subprofileId, seeds existingDrugs with that subprofile's active drug names. (2) When no subprofileId is supplied but a patientUserId was resolved, loops over EVERY subprofile of that patient and issues one query per subprofile (N+1). Results are concatenated with drug names pulled from the patient's active Prescriptions, deduped via `[...new Set(...)]` preserving first-seen order, and that ORDER IS VISIBLE in the response as `drugsChecked` (input medications first, then existing drugs). deletedAt is not filtered.
findings.portRecommendation: NEW method on IPatientDirectory (Patients module), batched to kill the N+1 while preserving order: Task<IReadOnlyList<string>> ListActiveMedicationNamesAsync(IReadOnlyCollection<string> subprofileIds, CancellationToken ct = default), ordered by subprofile id then insertion order. Do NOT expose full CurrentMedication rows — only the names cross the boundary.

findings.name: Allergy + ChronicCondition context read — BROKEN TODAY, always yields empty lists
findings.signature: prisma.allergy.findMany({ where: { subprofileId: subId, isActive: true }, select: { allergen: true } })  and  prisma.chronicCondition.findMany({ where: { subprofileId: subId, isActive: true }, select: { name: true } })
findings.behaviour: BOTH queries are invalid against the current schema. Allergy has NO isActive column (its fields are id, patientProfileId, subprofileId, allergen, severity, reaction, createdAt, updatedAt, deletedAt). ChronicCondition has isActive but NO `name` column — the field is `condition`. Prisma rejects both at validation time; they run inside Promise.all inside `try { ... } catch { /* continue without context */ }`, so the throw is swallowed and BOTH patientAllergies and patientConditions remain []. Net effect in production: the drug-interaction AI call has NEVER received allergy or condition context, and the failure is invisible (no log line). Compare visits.js:709-710, which reads the same data correctly via `c.condition` and an unfiltered allergies relation.
findings.portRecommendation: A .NET port that 'ports the intent' would silently CHANGE behaviour — the AI would suddenly get allergy/condition context and produce different interaction output. Recommendation: reproduce the empty-list outcome (pass empty PatientAllergies/PatientConditions to the interaction service) and raise this as a separate product decision. If it is fixed, do it behind IPatientDirectory.GetSubprofileClinicalContextAsync (Patients module) mapping Condition→the `condition` column and dropping the non-existent isActive filter on allergies — and expect the endpoint's AI output to change.

findings.name: Appointment.subprofileId read from inside the Visits module
findings.signature: prisma.appointment.findUnique({ where: { id: appointmentId }, select: { subprofileId: true } })
findings.behaviour: When the request body carries appointmentId and no explicit subprofileId, the appointment's subprofileId is auto-propagated onto the new Visit. Wrapped in `try { } catch { /* continue without */ }`. Note that appointmentId itself is NEVER persisted on the Visit — the Visit model has no appointmentId column (see the dead-code finding) — so this is the only trace the appointment leaves on the visit.
findings.portRecommendation: NEW port IAppointmentDirectory (Appointments module owns it, published in SharedKernel/Abstractions/Directory): Task<AppointmentSummary?> GetAppointmentAsync(string appointmentId, CancellationToken ct = default) with `sealed record AppointmentSummary(string Id, string ClinicId, string PhysicianId, string PatientUserId, string? SubprofileId, string? ClinicPatientId, string Status, DateTime AppointmentDate, string StartTime, string EndTime, string? Reason)`. Visits depends on this port, never on AppointmentsDbContext.

findings.name: DEAD CODE — visit.appointmentId does not exist, so two cross-module writes never fire
findings.signature: if (visit.appointmentId) { prisma.appointment.update({ ... status:'COMPLETED' }) }  and  prisma.payment.updateMany({ where: { appointmentId: visit.appointmentId, visitId: null }, data: { visitId: id } })
findings.behaviour: The Prisma Visit model (schema.prisma:617-676) has NO appointmentId field, so `visit.appointmentId` is always `undefined` and BOTH guarded blocks are unreachable. Consequences visible to the client today: completing a visit does NOT auto-complete the linked appointment (it stays PENDING/CONFIRMED in GET /appointments and in the queue), and the PENDING cash Payment created at check-in is NEVER linked to the visit (payment.visitId stays null). POST /visits also accepts appointmentId in the body and uses it only for the subprofile propagation above — it is never stored.
findings.portRecommendation: NO port required — do not implement these two branches. Porting them 'correctly' (by adding Visit.AppointmentId) would be a behaviour change the React client is not written against: appointments would start flipping to COMPLETED and payments would start linking. Record it as a known Node defect and route it through a product decision, not the port.

findings.name: Visit reads from inside the Appointments module (three distinct queries)
findings.signature: prisma.visit.count({ where: { clinicId, patientUserId, status:'COMPLETED' } });  prisma.visit.findMany({ where: { clinicId, visitDate: {gte,lte} }, select: { id, patientUserId, status, followUpDate, followUpNotes, completedAt } });  prisma.visit.findMany({ where: { physicianId, status:'COMPLETED', completedAt: { not: null }, visitDate: { gte } }, select: { visitDate, completedAt } })
findings.behaviour: (1) check-in: the count decides consultation vs follow-up fee (>0 → follow-up). (2) GET /queue: today's visits at the clinic are indexed BY patientUserId into a plain object — LAST WRITE WINS, so a patient with two visits the same day loses the earlier one — then merged onto each queue row as four NEW response keys: visitStatus (v.status or null), visitFollowUp (v.followUpDate or null), visitFollowUpNotes, visitCompletedAt. Rows with no matching visit get all four as explicit null. (3) ai-optimize: durations are computed as (completedAt - visitDate)/60000 minutes, filtered to 0 < d < 300, averaged with Math.round; if none survive, stats.avgVisitDurationMin is null. QUIRK across all three: NONE applies the deletedAt soft-delete filter, so archived/soft-deleted visits count toward the follow-up fee, the queue overlay and the duration stats.
findings.portRecommendation: NEW port IVisitDirectory (Visits module owns it, published in SharedKernel/Abstractions/Directory) with exactly three methods so Appointments never sees a Visit entity: Task<int> CountCompletedAsync(string clinicId, string patientUserId, CancellationToken ct = default); Task<IReadOnlyList<VisitQueueRow>> ListForClinicDayAsync(string clinicId, DateTime dayStartUtc, DateTime dayEndUtc, CancellationToken ct = default) → `record VisitQueueRow(string Id, string PatientUserId, string Status, DateTime? FollowUpDate, string? FollowUpNotes, DateTime? CompletedAt)`; Task<IReadOnlyList<VisitDuration>> ListCompletedDurationsAsync(string physicianProfileId, DateTime sinceUtc, CancellationToken ct = default) → `record VisitDuration(DateTime VisitDate, DateTime CompletedAt)`. All three must OMIT the deletedAt filter to stay faithful.

findings.name: Visit reads from inside the Prescriptions module (ownership, patient identity, and an embedded visit+clinic object)
findings.signature: where.visit = { patientUserId: userId };  prisma.visit.findFirst({ where: { id: visitId, physicianId } });  prisma.visit.findUnique({ where:{id}, select:{ patientUserId } });  include: { visit: { select: { id, chiefComplaint, visitDate, patientUserId, clinic: { select: {...} } } } }
findings.behaviour: Five distinct needs. (a) RELATION FILTER: the patient branch of GET /prescriptions filters prescriptions by `visit: { patientUserId }`, and check-interactions does the same — a cross-module SQL join that a DTO-returning port cannot express. (b) OWNERSHIP: POST / does visit.findFirst({id, physicianId}) → 403 {error:'Visit not found or not yours'}, and reads visit.subprofileId to copy onto the new Prescription. (c) IDENTITY: PUT /:id/send reads visit.patientUserId TWICE (two separate findUnique calls in two separate try blocks — the notification block and the reminder block); refill-request, refill-respond, stop-medication and resume-medication each include visit:{patientUserId} purely for the ownership check (it does NOT reach the response — those endpoints return projected subsets). (d) EMBEDDED OBJECT that DOES go out: GET /prescriptions → visit:{id,chiefComplaint,visitDate,patientUserId,clinic:{name}}; GET /prescriptions/:id → visit:{id,chiefComplaint,visitDate,patientUserId,clinic:{name,phone,address}}; POST /prescriptions → visit:{chiefComplaint,visitDate} (no id, no patientUserId); GET /:id/pdf → visit:{patientUserId,clinicPatientId,clinicPatient:{name},clinic:{name,address,city,phone,logo}} (HTML output). visitDate serializes as a full ISO string. (e) None of these filter Visit.deletedAt.
findings.portRecommendation: Extend the SAME IVisitDirectory (Visits module). Add: Task<IReadOnlyList<string>> ListVisitIdsForPatientAsync(string patientUserId, CancellationToken ct = default) — Prescriptions then filters `WHERE VisitId IN (...)` instead of joining, which is the only boundary-safe way to express the relation filter; Task<VisitSummary?> GetVisitAsync(string visitId, CancellationToken ct = default) and a batched Task<IReadOnlyDictionary<string, VisitSummary>> GetVisitsAsync(IReadOnlyCollection<string> visitIds, CancellationToken ct = default) with `sealed record VisitSummary(string Id, string ClinicId, string PhysicianId, string PatientUserId, string? SubprofileId, string? ClinicPatientId, string? ChiefComplaint, DateTime VisitDate)`. The nested `clinic` object must be assembled in the Prescriptions response DTO from IClinicDirectory (Prescriptions calls both ports) — do NOT let IVisitDirectory return a clinic graph, or Visits becomes a proxy for Clinics. Watch the ListVisitIdsForPatientAsync cardinality: for a long-tenured patient this IN-list can grow large; page it or push the filter into a Prescriptions-side denormalized PatientUserId column if the list exceeds SQL Server's parameter budget.

findings.name: Prescription reads from inside the Visits module — full rows and a relation count
findings.signature: _count: { select: { prescriptions: true, investigations: true } };  include: { prescriptions: true }
findings.behaviour: GET /visits emits `_count: { prescriptions: <int>, investigations: <int> }` on every row — the underscore-prefixed key is part of the wire contract, and it is present for BOTH the physician and the patient branches (the patient strip only removes subjective/objective/assessment/plan/rawNotes/rawTranscript/audioUrl). GET /visits/:id embeds `prescriptions: [ ...full rows... ]` — every Prescription column: id, visitId, physicianId, subprofileId, status, medications (Json array), notes, signedAt, sentToPatientAt, pdfUrl, refillRequestedAt, refillStatus, refillNotes, createdAt, updatedAt, deletedAt. Empty array (never null) when there are none. Neither the count nor the list filters deletedAt, so soft-deleted prescriptions are counted AND returned. GET /visits/:id also has a documented fallback: if the full include throws, it retries with only clinic+physician+prescriptions and then force-sets investigations=[] and subprofile=null.
findings.portRecommendation: NEW port IPrescriptionDirectory (Prescriptions module owns it, published in SharedKernel/Abstractions/Directory): Task<IReadOnlyDictionary<string, int>> CountByVisitAsync(IReadOnlyCollection<string> visitIds, CancellationToken ct = default) — one query for the whole page, returning 0 for visits with none; and Task<IReadOnlyList<PrescriptionRow>> ListByVisitAsync(string visitId, CancellationToken ct = default) returning a record with ALL sixteen columns above, including DeletedAt, since the JSON carries it. Investigation stays inside Visits (Tebrazi.Visits.Domain/Entities/Investigation.cs already exists) — no port needed for that half of the _count.

findings.name: User lookups for patient-name enrichment (batched and single)
findings.signature: prisma.user.findMany({ where: { id: { in: ids } }, select: { id, displayName, email|phone } });  prisma.user.findUnique({ where: { id }, select: { displayName[, email][, phone] } })
findings.behaviour: Five distinct projections reach the client and the key sets differ per endpoint: GET /visits → patientUser:{id,displayName,email}; GET /visits/:id → patientUser:{displayName,email,phone} (no id); GET /appointments → patientUser:{id,displayName,phone} (no email); GET /appointments/today → patientUser:{id,displayName}; GET /appointments/queue → patientUser:{displayName,phone} (no id); GET /prescriptions → NOT an object at all — it emits a flat `patientName: <string>` and, crucially, `patientMap[id] || undefined`, so the key is OMITTED from the JSON when the user is missing; GET /prescriptions/:id → patientUser:{displayName,email,phone}. Missing-user handling also differs: the appointment/visit list endpoints emit `patientUser: null`, GET /visits/:id emits whatever findUnique returns (null), and the prescriptions list omits the key. The remaining single lookups (visits complete/feedback/follow-ups, appointment booking/walk-in/check-in/intake/cancel, prescription send/refill/pdf) read only displayName for notification text and use `?.displayName || 'A patient'|'Patient'|'Your doctor'` fallbacks. PERF: GET /appointments/queue calls findUnique INSIDE a Promise.all(map) — one query per queue row (N+1).
findings.portRecommendation: COVERED by IIdentityDirectory.GetUsersAsync / GetUserAsync — UserSummary already carries Id, Email, DisplayName, Phone. No new port. Two rules for the .NET side: (1) never serialize UserSummary directly — each endpoint's response DTO must project the exact key subset listed above, and GET /prescriptions must OMIT patientName rather than emit null; (2) replace the GET /queue N+1 with the batched GetUsersAsync while keeping the per-row output identical.

findings.name: User.subscriptionTier + userType read by the AI usage limiter middleware — NOT covered by UserSummary
findings.signature: prisma.user.findUnique({ where: { id: userId }, select: { id: true, userType: true, subscriptionTier: true } })
findings.behaviour: Runs before POST /visits/:id/generate-soap, POST /visits/:id/transcribe, POST /visits/:id/suggest-codes and POST /prescriptions/transcribe-rx. Resolves a tier (PATIENT users are forced to PATIENT_FREE/PATIENT_FAMILY regardless of subscriptionTier), then rejects with 403 {error:'Feature not available on your plan', message, upgradeRequired:true, currentTier} for a disallowed agent, or 429 {error:'Monthly AI limit reached', message, upgradeRequired:true, currentTier, usage:{used,limit,totalTokens,totalCost,resetsAt}} over quota. On success it attaches req.aiUsage, which is serialized into the generate-soap response as `aiUsage: { used, limit, remaining, tier }`. WIRE QUIRK: for the CLINIC tier limit and remaining are JavaScript Infinity, and JSON.stringify(Infinity) is `null` — so the client receives `aiUsage: { used: 0, limit: null, remaining: null, tier: 'CLINIC' }`. The middleware also fails OPEN: any thrown error inside it calls next() and the request proceeds with req.aiUsage undefined, so generate-soap then emits `aiUsage: null`. It counts usage by aggregating AiAuditLog (userId, createdAt >= month start, success:true, cached:false).
findings.portRecommendation: GAP in the existing port: UserSummary has no SubscriptionTier. Recommend extending IIdentityDirectory rather than creating a second identity port — either add `string SubscriptionTier` to UserSummary (touches every existing consumer) or add Task<string?> GetSubscriptionTierAsync(string userId, CancellationToken ct = default). Owned by Identity. The AiAuditLog metering itself belongs in a cross-cutting IAiUsageMeter in SharedKernel (not in any of the three modules), since it is middleware, and its C# DTO must emit null — not double.PositiveInfinity — for the CLINIC tier.

findings.name: Notification creation — 12 distinct notification types raised across the three files
findings.signature: createNotification({ userId, type, title, message, data, sendEmail?, sendPush? }) → prisma.notification.create({ data: { userId, type, title, message, data } })
findings.behaviour:
Types raised: FOLLOW_UP_SET, VISIT_COMPLETED (sendEmail:true), VISIT_COMPLETED_STAFF, PATIENT_FEEDBACK, FOLLOW_UP_REMINDER (sendEmail:false, sendPush:false), NEW_APPOINTMENT_REQUEST (sendEmail:true), PATIENT_ARRIVED (×2 — walk-in and check-in), APPOINTMENT_CONFIRMED (sendEmail:true), APPOINTMENT_CANCELLED (×2 — one to physician, one to patient with sendEmail:true), INTAKE_NOTE_READY, PRESCRIPTION_SENT (sendEmail:true), MEDICATION_REMINDER_SET, REFILL_REQUEST, REFILL_RESPONSE (sendEmail:true). NOTE: several of these (VISIT_COMPLETED_STAFF, PATIENT_FEEDBACK, FOLLOW_UP_SET, NEW_APPOINTMENT_REQUEST, MEDICATION_REMINDER_SET, REFILL_REQUEST, REFILL_RESPONSE, APPOINTMENT_REMINDER) are NOT in the service's own NOTIFICATION_TYPES whitelist — the list is documentation only and is never enforced, so the type column accepts anything. Side effects inside createNotification: when sendEmail it re-reads the User (email, displayName) and sends `

{title}

{message}

`; push is ALWAYS attempted regardless of sendPush (the parameter is accepted and ignored). Every call site wraps it in a swallowing try/catch — a notification failure must never fail the request or change the response. Message strings embed locale-formatted dates (toLocaleDateString('en-US', {...}) in some places, bare toLocaleDateString() in others) and must be reproduced character-for-character.
findings.portRecommendation: NEW port, cross-cutting rather than module-owned. Publish INotificationDispatcher in SharedKernel/Abstractions/Notifications: Task<string> CreateAsync(NotificationRequest request, CancellationToken ct = default) with `sealed record NotificationRequest(string UserId, string Type, string Title, string Message, object? Data = null, bool SendEmail = false, bool SendPush = false)`. Since no Notifications module exists in .NET yet, create one (Tebrazi.Notifications) to own the notifications table plus the email/push fan-out; the three modules depend only on the interface. The implementation must swallow its own failures so call sites can stay try-free.

findings.name: Notification READ — once-per-day dedupe via a Postgres JSON path query
findings.signature: prisma.notification.findFirst({ where: { userId, type: 'FOLLOW_UP_REMINDER', data: { path: ['visitId'], equals: visit.id }, createdAt: { gte: today } } })
findings.behaviour: The only cross-module notification READ. For each overdue follow-up it checks whether a FOLLOW_UP_REMINDER already exists TODAY for that visit before sending, giving once-per-day-per-visit semantics. `today` is local midnight (new Date(y, m, d)), not UTC. The filter reaches INSIDE the Json `data` column for the `visitId` key — a Prisma/Postgres JSON path predicate. The loop is sequential (await per overdue visit) and runs on a GET request that is also wrapped in cacheMiddleware(30), so the side effect only fires on a cache miss.
findings.portRecommendation: NEW method on the same INotificationDispatcher (or a sibling INotificationQuery in SharedKernel): Task<bool> ExistsSinceAsync(string userId, string type, string dataKey, string dataValue, DateTime sinceUtc, CancellationToken ct = default), owned by the new Notifications module. The SQL Server implementation must translate the JSON path to JSON_VALUE([Data], '$.visitId') = @value — EF's built-in Json mapping will not produce the Postgres form. Keep the local-midnight boundary, not UTC midnight.

findings.name: WaitingQueue reads and writes from Visits and Appointments
findings.signature: prisma.waitingQueue.updateMany / findFirst / create
findings.behaviour: Three operations, all in swallowing try/catch, none reaching the response body. (1) Visits PUT /:id/complete: updateMany({ clinicId, patientUserId, queueDate between local day bounds, status in ['WAITING','BEING_SEEN'] }, { status:'COMPLETED', completedAt: now }) — auto-closes the queue entry. (2) Appointments POST /walk-in: findFirst for an existing WAITING/BEING_SEEN entry today; if none, findFirst ordered by queueNumber desc to compute `(last?.queueNumber || 0) + 1`, then resolves the physician's userId and (when subprofileId is present) the subprofile name, and creates an entry with source:'APPOINTMENT', appointmentId, reason: reason||'Walk-in', patientName = subprofile name if any else user displayName else 'Patient', subprofileName = subprofile name or null. (3) Appointments PUT /:id/check-in: the same existence check + queueNumber allocation, creating with physicianUserId from appt.physician.user.id, patientName from the User lookup, reason: appt.reason || null, and NO subprofile handling (unlike walk-in). RACE: queueNumber is allocated with a read-then-write and no unique constraint — two concurrent check-ins produce duplicate numbers.
findings.portRecommendation: NEW port IWaitingQueueService, and a NEW module to own it (Tebrazi.WaitingRoom — the table has no .NET home). Publish in SharedKernel/Abstractions: Task CompleteForPatientAsync(string clinicId, string patientUserId, DateTime dayStartLocal, DateTime dayEndLocal, CancellationToken ct = default) and Task<int?> EnqueueIfAbsentAsync(WaitingQueueEntry entry, CancellationToken ct = default) returning the allocated queue number or null when the patient was already queued, with `sealed record WaitingQueueEntry(string ClinicId, string PhysicianUserId, string? PatientUserId, string? SubprofileId, string? SubprofileName, string PatientName, string Source, string? AppointmentId, string? Reason, DateTime QueueDateLocal)`. Push queue-number allocation inside the port so the race can be fixed there without changing any caller.

findings.name: Payment read + write from the check-in endpoint
findings.signature: prisma.payment.findFirst({ where: { appointmentId: id } });  prisma.payment.create({ data: { clinicId, physicianId, patientUserId, appointmentId, amount, currency:'EGP', method:'CASH', description, status:'PENDING' } })
findings.behaviour: Egyptian cash-first flow: the receptionist collects before the doctor is seen. Creates a PENDING CASH payment only when no Payment row exists for the appointment AND the resolved fee > 0. description is 'Follow-up visit fee' or 'Consultation fee'. THE RESULT IS IN THE RESPONSE: PUT /:id/check-in returns `payment: { id, amount, description }` on creation, and `payment: null` when the block was skipped, the clinic was missing, a payment already existed, the fee was 0, or anything threw. The visits.js counterpart (payment.updateMany to backfill visitId) is unreachable dead code — see the visit.appointmentId finding.
findings.portRecommendation: NEW port IPaymentService, owned by a NEW Tebrazi.Payments module (payments/invoices have no .NET home yet). Publish in SharedKernel/Abstractions: Task<PaymentCreated?> EnsureCheckInPaymentAsync(CheckInPaymentRequest request, CancellationToken ct = default) returning `sealed record PaymentCreated(string Id, double Amount, string? Description)` or null. Putting the 'already exists / fee > 0' guard inside the port keeps the idempotency in one place and keeps Appointments free of Payment entities.

findings.name: PatientNote upsert from the intake-note endpoint — and a unique-constraint bug
findings.signature: prisma.patientNote.findFirst({ where: { physicianUserId, patientUserId, content: { startsWith: '[INTAKE]' } } }); then patientNote.update or patientNote.create({ data: { physicianUserId, patientUserId, content } })
findings.behaviour: BUG: the search predicate is startsWith('[INTAKE]') but the written content is `[INTAKE by ${userId}]\n${note}` — '[INTAKE by abc]'.startsWith('[INTAKE]') is FALSE, so the findFirst never matches its own writes and the handler always takes the create branch. PatientNote carries @@unique([physicianUserId, patientUserId, subprofileId]) and subprofileId is left null, so the SECOND intake note for the same physician+patient pair violates the unique index → Prisma P2002 → the catch returns 500 {error:'Failed to save intake note'}. The endpoint therefore works exactly once per physician-patient pair. Response on success: `{ ...savedNote, message: 'Intake note saved' }` — the full PatientNote row (id, physicianUserId, patientUserId, subprofileId, clinicPatientId, content, isPinned, createdAt, updatedAt) plus the message key. physicianUserId resolves to the caller when they are the physician, otherwise to appt.physician.user.id.
findings.portRecommendation: NEW port IPatientNoteService owned by a NEW Tebrazi.PatientNotes (or CRM) module — PatientNote/PatientTag have no .NET home. Publish: Task<PatientNoteRow> UpsertIntakeNoteAsync(string physicianUserId, string patientUserId, string content, CancellationToken ct = default). Reproduce the failure mode deliberately or fix it as a flagged product decision — a naive C# upsert would silently change behaviour from '500 on the second note' to 'overwrite', which is arguably correct but is NOT what the client is written against.

findings.name: Reminder deleteMany + create fan-out when a prescription is sent
findings.signature: prisma.reminder.deleteMany({ where: { userId, type:'MEDICATION', title: { contains: drugName }, status:'ACTIVE' } });  prisma.reminder.create({ data: { userId, createdById, title, description, type:'MEDICATION', remindAt, recurrence:'DAILY', prescriptionId, notes } })
findings.behaviour: For each medication with both frequency and drugName: parseFrequency(med.frequency) yields {dosesPerDay,intervalHours}; getDefaultDoseTimes(dosesPerDay) yields HH:mm strings; existing ACTIVE MEDICATION reminders whose title CONTAINS the drug name are hard-deleted (a substring match — 'Metformin' also nukes 'Metformin XR'); then one DAILY reminder per dose time is created. remindAt is today at that time, rolled to TOMORROW when the time has already passed. title is `💊 ${drugName}${doseLabel}` where doseLabel is '' for a single dose and ` (Dose ${i+1}/${dosesPerDay})` otherwise — the emoji is part of the stored string. description is `${dosage ? dosage + ' — ' : ''}Take at ${timeStr}` with timeStr from toLocaleTimeString('en-US',{hour:'2-digit',minute:'2-digit',hour12:true}). notes is a JSON STRING (JSON.stringify of {drugName,dosage,frequency,doseNumber,totalDoses,intervalHours}) in a plain String? column. When remindersCreated > 0 a MEDICATION_REMINDER_SET notification follows. The whole block is in a swallowing try/catch and never affects the response, which is `{ ...updated, message: 'Prescription sent to patient' }`.
findings.portRecommendation: NEW port IReminderService owned by a NEW Tebrazi.Reminders module (no .NET home). Publish: Task<int> ReplaceMedicationRemindersAsync(string patientUserId, string createdByUserId, string prescriptionId, IReadOnlyList<MedicationSchedule> schedules, CancellationToken ct = default) returning the count created, with `record MedicationSchedule(string DrugName, string? Dosage, string Frequency)`. Keep parseFrequency/getDefaultDoseTimes (server/src/utils/medicationScheduleUtils.js) INSIDE the Reminders module — the title/description/notes strings are the reminder module's format, not the prescription module's, and Prescriptions should hand over drug data, not formatted text.

findings.name: InventoryItem read + InventoryTransaction write on dispense
findings.signature: prisma.inventoryItem.findUnique({ where: { id: itemId } });  prisma.$transaction([ inventoryItem.update({ currentStock: { decrement: qty } }), inventoryTransaction.create({...}) ]);  compensating inventoryItem.update({ currentStock: { increment: qty } })
findings.behaviour: Runs only when the body carries a non-empty inventoryItems array of {itemId, quantity}. Per item: skip if !itemId || !quantity; fetch the item and skip if missing or !isActive; atomically decrement stock and write an InventoryTransaction {itemId, type:'DISPENSED', quantity: -qty, previousStock: item.currentStock, newStock: Math.max(0, item.currentStock - qty), prescriptionId, notes:'Dispensed via prescription', performedById: req.user.id}. If the post-decrement stock is negative, a COMPENSATING increment runs and the item is skipped — but the InventoryTransaction row is NOT deleted, so a phantom DISPENSED transaction is left behind. IN THE RESPONSE: `{ ...updated, message:'Prescription dispensed', inventoryDeducted: [ { itemId, name, quantity, newStock } ] }` — an empty array (never null) when nothing was deducted. Note the whole thing runs with NO try/catch of its own: an inventory failure DOES 500 the request, after the prescription has already been marked DISPENSED.
findings.portRecommendation: NEW port IInventoryService owned by a NEW Tebrazi.Inventory module (no .NET home; the Node routes live in server/src/routes/inventory.js). Publish: Task<IReadOnlyList<InventoryDeduction>> DispenseAsync(string prescriptionId, string performedByUserId, IReadOnlyList<InventoryRequestLine> lines, CancellationToken ct = default) with `record InventoryRequestLine(string ItemId, int Quantity)` and `record InventoryDeduction(string ItemId, string Name, int Quantity, int NewStock)`. Move the negative-stock compensation inside the port and preserve the orphaned-transaction quirk (or fix it as a flagged decision) — and keep the exception propagating, since the 500-after-DISPENSED ordering is observable.

findings.name: InteractionAlert — read and write, and where it belongs
findings.signature: prisma.interactionAlert.findMany({ where: { physicianId }, orderBy: { checkedAt: 'desc' }, take: limit });  prisma.interactionAlert.create({ data: { physicianId, patientUserId, drugs, interactions, alertCount } })
findings.behaviour: GET /interaction-history returns FULL rows: [{ id, physicianId, patientUserId, visitId, drugs (Json array), interactions (Json array), alertCount, checkedAt (ISO string) }], newest first, take = parseInt(req.query.limit) || 20 with NO upper bound (a caller can request the whole table). Returns [] when the caller has no physician profile. The create in check-interactions sets physicianId to the caller's profile id OR null, and patientUserId to req.user.id ONLY when the caller is not a physician (mutually exclusive), leaving visitId always null even when visitId was supplied in the body. It is wrapped in a swallowing try/catch, so a logging failure does not affect the interaction response.
findings.portRecommendation: NO cross-module port needed — InteractionAlert has no relations and is only ever touched from prescriptions.js. Recommend the PRESCRIPTIONS module own the table outright (Tebrazi.Prescriptions.Domain/Entities/InteractionAlert.cs plus a store on IPrescriptionStores). Note the unbounded `limit` as a hardening item, but cap it only as a deliberate, flagged change — the current contract has no cap.

findings.name: ActivityLog and AiAuditLog writes from middleware attached to these routes
findings.file: server/src/middleware/audit.js (applied at visits.js:182 POST /, prescriptions.js:99 POST /); server/src/services/aiUsageLimiter.js + aiGateway (applied at visits.js:674,964,1023 and prescriptions.js:972)
findings.signature: prisma.activityLog.create({ data: { userId, action, resource, resourceId, metadata, ipAddress, userAgent } }).catch(()=>{});  prisma.aiAuditLog.aggregate/groupBy/create
findings.behaviour: auditLog('CREATE','visit') and auditLog('CREATE','prescription') monkey-patch res.json to log AFTER the response is composed: only when statusCode < 400 and req.user?.id exists; resourceId = req.params?.id || data?.id || null; metadata = { method, path: req.originalUrl, ...(req.body?.reason ? { reason } : {}) }; userAgent truncated to 256 chars; fire-and-forget with a bare .catch so it can never fail or delay the response. AiAuditLog is aggregated for quota counting (userId, createdAt >= month start, success:true, cached:false) and written by the AI gateway on every call. Neither table is visible in any response body.
findings.portRecommendation: NOT module ports — cross-cutting infrastructure. Publish IAuditTrail (Task LogAsync(AuditEntry entry, CancellationToken ct)) and IAiUsageMeter in SharedKernel/Abstractions, implemented in Tebrazi.Infrastructure.Shared, and wire them as ASP.NET middleware/filters exactly as the Express middleware is wired — an ActionFilter that inspects the result AFTER the handler, writing fire-and-forget. Do NOT let Visits or Prescriptions inject an audit DbContext.

findings.name: Soft-delete and cache quirks that cut across every port above
findings.file: visits.js:15,89 (softDeleteFilter); appointments.js:352,511 and prescriptions.js:31,144 (cacheMiddleware); server/src/lib/queryHelpers.js, server/src/lib/cacheMiddleware.js
findings.signature: const softDeleteFilter = { deletedAt: null };  cacheMiddleware(ttl) keyed by `route:${userId}:${req.originalUrl}`
findings.behaviour: SOFT DELETE IS INCONSISTENT and the inconsistency is observable. Only GET /visits applies `{ deletedAt: null }`. Every other query in all three files omits it: GET /visits/:id, the prescription count and prescription list embedded in visits, all Appointment queries (Appointment HAS a deletedAt column), all Prescription queries (Prescription HAS deletedAt — and GET /visits/:id returns the deletedAt field itself in each embedded prescription row), and all three Visit reads from the Appointments module. Visits additionally have a SECOND soft-delete channel: DELETE /visits/:id sets status='ARCHIVED' (not deletedAt), physicians are filtered with `status: { not: 'ARCHIVED' }` when no status filter is given, patients see `status in ['COMPLETED','ARCHIVED']`, and patients additionally filter `patientDismissedAt: null`. CACHING: cacheMiddleware wraps GET /appointments (15s), GET /appointments/today (15s), GET /prescriptions (15s), GET /prescriptions/summary (30s), GET /visits/follow-ups-due (30s). The key is (userId, originalUrl) and IGNORES the X-Clinic-Id header — but GET /appointments branches on that header to decide clinic-staff scoping, so a staff member switching clinics can be served the previous clinic's list for up to 15 seconds. GET /visits/follow-ups-due also has SIDE EFFECTS (it sends FOLLOW_UP_REMINDER notifications), which therefore fire only on a cache miss.
findings.portRecommendation: No port of its own, but a hard rule for every port implementation listed above: each method must state whether it filters DeletedAt, and must match the Node query exactly. Recommend a global EF query filter is NOT used for Visit/Appointment/Prescription — a blanket HasQueryFilter(x => x.DeletedAt == null) would silently change GET /visits/:id, the _count, the check-in follow-up fee and the ai-optimize stats. Apply the filter per-query, only where Node applies it. For caching, key the .NET response cache on (userId, path, query, X-Clinic-Id) or drop caching on GET /appointments — and move the follow-ups-due notification side effect out of the cached GET path.
